title: The N-terminal domain of the human mitochondrial helicase Twinkle has DNA binding activity crucial for supporting processive DNA synthesis by Polymerase γ
authors: Laura C. Johnson; Anupam Singh; Smita S. Patel
one_liner_zh: 该文通过生化实验表征人线粒体解旋酶Twinkle的N端结构域DNA结合活性及其对Polγ合成的作用，虽涉及蛋白-DNA互作但无AI/物理模拟方法，且非TF-DNA体系，仅部分相关。
abstract: Twinkle is the ring-shaped replicative helicase within the human mitochondria with high homology to bacteriophage T7 gp4 helicase-primase. Unlike many orthologs of Twinkle, the N-terminal domain (NTD) of human Twinkle has lost its primase activity through evolutionarily acquired mutations. The NTD has demonstrated no observed activity thus far, hence its role has remained unclear. In this study, we have biochemically characterized the isolated NTD and C-terminal domain with linker (CTD) to decipher their contributions to the activities of the full-length (FL) Twinkle. This novel CTD construct hydrolyzes ATP, has weak DNA unwinding activity, and assists Polγ-catalyzed strand-displacement synthesis on short replication forks. However, CTD fails to promote multi-kilobase length product formation by Polγ in rolling-circle DNA synthesis. Thus, CTD retains all the motor functions but struggles to implement them for processive translocation. We show that NTD has DNA binding activity, and its presence stabilizes Twinkle oligomerization. The CTD oligomerizes on its own, but loss of NTD results in heterogeneously-sized oligomeric species. The CTD also exhibits weaker and salt-sensitive DNA binding compared to FL Twinkle. Based on these results, we propose that NTD directly contributes to DNA binding and holds the DNA in place behind the central channel of the CTD like a ‘doorstop’, preventing helicase slippages and sustaining processive unwinding. Consistent with this model, mtSSB compensate for the NTD loss and partially restore kilobase length DNA synthesis by CTD and Polγ. The implications of our studies are foundational for understanding the mechanisms of disease-causing Twinkle mutants that lie in the NTD.
abstract_zh: Twinkle是人类线粒体内环状复制解旋酶，与噬菌体T7 gp4解旋酶-引物酶具有高度同源性。与Twinkle的许多直系同源物不同，人类Twinkle的N端结构域（NTD）通过进化性获得的突变失去了其引物酶活性。迄今为止，NTD未观察到任何活性，因此其作用仍不清楚。在本研究中，我们对分离的NTD和带有接头的C端结构域（CTD）进行了生化表征，以阐明它们对全长（FL）Twinkle活性的贡献。这种新型CTD构建体能水解ATP，具有较弱的DNA解旋活性，并能辅助Polγ在短复制叉上催化链置换合成。然而，CTD无法促进Polγ在滚环DNA合成中生成多千碱基长度的产物。因此，CTD保留了所有马达功能，但难以将其用于持续性转位。我们表明NTD具有DNA结合活性，其存在稳定了Twinkle的寡聚化。CTD能自行寡聚化，但NTD的缺失导致寡聚体种类大小不均一。与FL Twinkle相比，CTD还表现出较弱的DNA结合能力且对盐敏感。基于这些结果，我们提出NTD直接参与DNA结合，并像“门挡”一样将DNA固定在CTD中央通道后方，防止解旋酶滑动并维持持续性解旋。与此模型一致，mtSSB能补偿NTD的缺失，并部分恢复CTD和Polγ的千碱基长度DNA合成。我们的研究意义在于为理解位于NTD中致病性Twinkle突变体的机制奠定基础。
